correctness.rationale: Every non-injective reduced essential closed m-walk would contain a smaller simple cycle, ruled out by girth at least m-1; walks with backtracks are null. Every simple m-cycle traversal is frozen because two distinct common neighbors give a forbidden 4-cycle. The exact count and regular D_m orbits then follow. Matsushita Theorem 5.8 and Lemma 5.11, inspected at the main proof in the open-access full text, identify null-component homotopy and count. Eight reconstructed finite examples and five independent cellular Euler counts corroborate, but are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: For a natural sharp high-girth range, one can recover the exact number of simple even cycles from a rational equivariant topological invariant of the Hom complex. The theorem gives a uniform full component count and primitive regular integral dihedral representation, not merely a possible list of homotopy types. The girth m-1 barrier is genuinely necessary by explicit counterfamily, and examples include noncyclic branched and nonbipartite graphs.
